Skipping meditation when life gets too busy
Adopting a spiritual path without a teacher
Believing spiritual growth replaces therapy entirely
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines spiritual bypassing as using spiritual ideas and practices to sidestep unresolved wounds and emotional issues.

questions.q: Why can trying to let go of the ego backfire?
a: It can inflate low self-esteem instead of healing it
It can make people arrogant about their progress
It can weaken the immune system over time
It can make people too selfish to help others
questions.why: Lesson 1 says when a low view of yourself meets the aim of killing the ego, it can inflate the problem rather than cure it.

questions.q: What does a healthy ego help you do?
a: Choose fitting goals and set boundaries in relationships
Ignore other people's needs and opinions completely
Avoid all criticism and conflict at work
Feel superior to people with less confidence
questions.why: Lesson 2 says ego awareness helps you pick goals that fit you and reveals what compromises you can and cannot make.

questions.q: How does Brzosko suggest you start befriending your ego?
a: Notice the feelings you learned to suppress
Argue back against your negative thoughts
Meditate until the ego becomes silent
Replace every bad feeling with a positive one
questions.why: Lesson 3 says unexpressed emotions create an unhealthy ego, so giving those feelings attention is the first step.

questions.q: What does befriending your ego mean?
a: Being at peace with it without overidentifying with it
Removing it entirely through meditation
Following its impulses without questioning them
Treating it as an enemy you must defeat
questions.why: The overview defines befriending the ego as being at peace with it without overidentifying with it.
